title: How the Odessa jazz party works
summary: Leeman describes the six-day invitation-only party held in west Texas, with 20 to 25 players, four-hour nights and lavish hospitality from wealthy sponsors.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: I believe their first party was in 1966. Their party is a beautiful, intimate and it's six days long, instead of the three day short parties of other people -- that other people hold -- and it is held in the unique Inn of the Golden West Hotel, and our wives, girlfriends, what have you, are always the guests of the committee and the Odessa Committee.

Also, they keep their list of musical artists to only about 20 to 25 players, which makes the party more intimate -- it doesn't get too cluttered up. We play four hours a night -- that's the schedule, but we run over, you know, it's hard to cut off the sets late because the musical excitement reaches tremendous peaks.
Then, we are wined and dined each night by the wealthy sponsors at their homes. They have bank Presidents, famous doctors, surgeons, owners of oil wells -- I'm getting envious -- and what have you.

They don't make the mistake of just saying in Texas -- it is West Texas, by God. They don't associate their higher plateau territory with the lower country of Houston, Dallas, Fort Worth and so on. Everyone has heard of southern hospitality, but if you've never had the Odessa, Midland west Texas treatment, you've never lived! Ask any musician lucky enough to be asked to play there.
